newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador shuts top cement-maker for price hike.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador shuts top cement-maker for price hike.

text.p: Ecuador's President Abdala Bucaram Thursday closed down the country's leading cement producer, Cemento Nacional, for marking up prices without government authorization.

"The president has ordered the closure of Cemento Nacional for raising the price of a cement sack by 1,000 sucres without authorization, and because that measure will directly affect the housing plan 'A Single Touch'," said a press release from the presidential office.
It said Bucaram had acted on the advice of Housing Minister Victor Sicuoret, who noted the cement price hike would push up costs for the government's ambitious housing plan by $2.0 million.

"Increasing the price of cement hurts the working class and boosts the profits of Cemento Nacional," Bucaram said. "The sale of cement is not ruled by the law of supply and demand, and therefore the industry is a monopoly."
Cemento Nacional officials declined to comment on the measure. But a company lawyer said he was studying the constitution to see whether the move was legal.
